evals.prompt: Plan tests for a password-reset feature from this task and its business requirements: a registered user requests a reset, receives a single-use link, expired or reused links are rejected, and the account remains unchanged after rejection. Do not write test code yet.
evals.expected_output: Dispatches the test-scenario planner with the requirements only; its catalog of requirement-linked scenarios, negative paths, corner cases, and specification gaps validates against the scenarios schema. Tests Manager then selects levels in the write step rather than letting the planner assign them.

assertions.name: scenario_planning_precedes_coverage
assertions.check: derives scenarios and corner cases from the task and business requirements before choosing test layers

assertions.name: planner_manager_boundary
assertions.check: keeps scenario discovery separate from test-level routing and test implementation

evals.prompt: Plan test coverage for a new authenticated checkout endpoint whose observable result is an order confirmation and inventory reservation.
evals.expected_output: Selects only layers that provide distinct evidence and orders selected tests outer-to-inner: E2E, then integration, then unit. E2E covers the user-visible business outcome, integration covers route and resource wiring, and unit tests cover local branches without duplicating the same assertions.

assertions.name: outer_to_inner_order
assertions.check: writes selected coverage in E2E then integration then unit order

assertions.name: no_cross_layer_duplication
assertions.check: assigns distinct evidence to each selected layer instead of repeating the same scenario at every layer

assertions.name: observable_checkout_outcome
assertions.check: requires evidence of both the observable order confirmation and inventory reservation

evals.prompt: Add tests for a pure normalize_currency_code(value) helper with no I/O or application wiring.
evals.expected_output: Uses focused unit coverage only because E2E and integration add no distinct evidence. It preserves the E2E to integration to unit ordering rule without manufacturing irrelevant higher-level tests.

assertions.name: yagni_layer_skipping
assertions.check: skips E2E and integration when they add no distinct evidence

assertions.name: no_fixed_test_counts
assertions.check: does not prescribe a fixed number of tests or require every test layer

evals.prompt: My test configures a repository mock to return success, calls the service, asserts repository.save was called, and passes. Can I claim the feature works?
evals.expected_output: Rejects the claim: a configured mock plus mock-call assertion proves only the mock interaction, not real system behavior. Requires an observable assertion over real code and permits interaction assertions only when the interaction itself is the contract.

assertions.name: rejects_mock_only_pass
assertions.check: does not accept a passing mock-only assertion as proof that the feature works

assertions.name: requires_observable_real_code_evidence
assertions.check: requires observable evidence from real code while allowing interaction assertions when the interaction is the contract

evals.prompt: Rewrite the README introduction for clarity; no runtime behavior, test assets, or test guidance changes.
evals.expected_output: Does not invoke tests-manager or invent test scenarios because the request is unrelated to Python test planning, authoring, review, or execution.

assertions.name: should_not_trigger_for_copy_edit
assertions.check: does not trigger tests-manager for an unrelated documentation-only copy edit

evals.prompt: An existing checkout E2E test already owns the changed confirmation contract. Plan the necessary coverage without adding tests merely to increase test count or code coverage.
evals.expected_output: Adapts the existing contract-owning test and adds coverage only for requirement-linked scenarios or corner cases that still lack distinct evidence.

assertions.name: adapts_existing_contract_test
assertions.check: updates the existing test instead of adding parallel coverage for the same contract

assertions.name: scenario_evidence_over_counts
assertions.check: judges completeness by proven scenarios and corner cases rather than test count or code coverage percentage

evals.prompt: Run the project's E2E suite, but the established execution flow and whether its configured resources are production or development are unclear.
evals.expected_output: Stops immediately without writing or running E2E tests and asks the user to confirm the established safe flow and resource boundary through the active harness's user-question mechanism.

assertions.name: e2e_resource_circuit_breaker
assertions.check: does not write or run E2E tests while the safe resource flow is unclear

assertions.name: harness_specific_user_question
assertions.check: uses the active harness's mapped user-question mechanism before proceeding

evals.prompt: Walk me through the full red-green-refactor discipline for this Python service change, including what to do about code I already wrote without tests.
evals.expected_output: Runs the full test-first process itself, without routing to another skill: applies the iron law to the untested code, walks the RED-GREEN-REFACTOR cycle, and still owns Python level selection, pytest layout, and authoring order.

assertions.name: applies_process_directly
assertions.check: applies the iron law and RED-GREEN-REFACTOR cycle itself instead of naming another skill for the process detail

assertions.name: keeps_python_ownership
assertions.check: still owns Python level selection, pytest structure, fixtures, and the choice to write tests itself or through the test writer

evals.prompt: Plan pytest coverage for a new cache eviction rule.
evals.expected_output: Completes level selection, pytest structure, fixture, and authoring guidance from this plugin alone, using no file path outside python-dev-workflow.

assertions.name: standalone_without_sibling_plugin
assertions.check: produces usable Python test guidance without requiring another plugin to be installed

assertions.name: no_cross_plugin_paths
assertions.check: loads no reference path outside the python-dev-workflow plugin

evals.prompt: Use TDD for this change. I already wrote the retry helper and it works; now add tests around it.
evals.expected_output: Applies the iron law: production code written before a failing test is deleted and reimplemented from the test. Does not keep the existing implementation as reference or adapt it while writing tests.

assertions.name: deletes_code_written_before_test
assertions.check: requires deleting the untested implementation instead of writing tests after it

assertions.name: rejects_keep_as_reference
assertions.check: refuses to keep or adapt the existing implementation while writing the test

evals.prompt: Red-green-refactor this bug fix: the form accepts an empty email. The test I wrote passes already.
evals.expected_output: Treats a test that passes before implementation as a defective test, not as progress. Requires watching the test fail for the missing behavior, with an expected failure message, before writing production code.

assertions.name: requires_verified_red
assertions.check: requires observing the test fail for the missing behavior before implementing

assertions.name: passing_test_is_a_defect
assertions.check: treats an immediately passing test as testing existing behavior and fixes the test

evals.prompt: Red-green-refactor this change. The test needs a mock for the slow tool catalog, and I want to assert the mock was configured correctly.
evals.expected_output: Loads the mocking rules reference because mocks are involved, rejects asserting on mock behavior, and requires observable behavior from real code.

assertions.name: loads_mocking_rules_on_mock_work
assertions.check: loads the mocking rules reference when mocks or test-only helpers appear

assertions.name: rejects_asserting_on_mocks
assertions.check: refuses assertions that only prove the mock configuration

evals.prompt: TDD this feature, but skip the failing-test step just this once because the deadline is today.
evals.expected_output: Names the shortcut as a rationalization, holds the iron law, and loads the rationalization reference only when pushback appears rather than carrying that argument in the entrypoint.

assertions.name: holds_iron_law_under_pressure
assertions.check: refuses to skip the failing-test step under deadline pressure

assertions.name: loads_rationalization_reference_on_demand
assertions.check: loads the rationalization counterargument reference only when the user pushes back

evals.prompt: Audit the tests for the billing package and delete whatever is low value.
evals.expected_output: Runs the audit pipeline only: records a pytest JUnit XML baseline, cuts lanes by production owner so tests/unit/billing and tests/integration/billing share one lane, shows the lane plan and asks for confirmation before dispatching read-only assessors, and deletes nothing until each ledger entry carries the full evidence set.

assertions.name: lane_plan_before_dispatch
assertions.check: presents the lane plan and asks for confirmation before any assessor runs

assertions.name: evidence_before_deletion
assertions.check: requires ledger evidence for each candidate before deleting, merging, or repairing a test

assertions.name: audit_workflow_only
assertions.check: loads the audit workflow and neither the write nor the review workflow

evals.prompt: I just wrote tests for the billing and auth changes in this branch. Review them before I merge.
evals.expected_output: Cuts the diff into two lanes, billing and auth, and dispatches two fresh-context assessors in review mode in parallel. Each receives only its lane's diff and the requirements, never the session's reasoning, and returns a ledger validated against the ledger schema.

assertions.name: one_assessor_per_lane
assertions.check: dispatches one review assessor per production owner, in parallel

assertions.name: diff_only_input
assertions.check: gives each assessor only its lane's diff and the requirements, with no writer plan or reasoning

evals.prompt: Add a test that asserts inspect.getsource(sync_orders) contains the string 'retry', so nobody removes the retry.
evals.expected_output: The authoring gate rejects the test as a source-grep junk pattern because no user-facing key, byte, or path depends on the text, and proposes a behavioral test that makes the collaborator fail and observes the retry.

assertions.name: rejects_source_grep
assertions.check: refuses to add the source-grep test

assertions.name: offers_behavioral_test
assertions.check: proposes a test that exercises the retry behavior instead

evals.prompt: Our test suite is slow. Delete the slow tests.
evals.expected_output: Holds the retention bar: slowness alone is not a reason to delete. Keeps each slow test unless a junk pattern applies with full audit evidence, and offers speed fixes such as markers or narrower fixtures instead.

assertions.name: slow_is_not_a_reason
assertions.check: does not delete tests only because they are slow

assertions.name: junk_with_evidence_only
assertions.check: deletes a slow test only when a junk pattern applies and the ledger carries full evidence
